slides.0.title: San Juan, San Rafael and Patagonia
slides.0.subtitle: San Juan, San Rafael and the cool regions of Río Negro and Neuquén
slides.1.title: San Juan
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.0.content: About 45,000 ha, roughly 25% of national wine volume and 20% of vineyard area, second only to Mendoza (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Climate and the Zonda
slides.1.highlights.1.content: About 150 mm of rain and roughly 330 sunny days; the Zonda blows mainly May–November, can lift temperatures 10–15°C within hours and suppresses mildew
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Sub-regions
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Tulum (about 25,000 ha at 600–650 m), Zonda, Ullum, Pedernal (1,300–1,400 m, about 850 ha, GI in 2007) and Calingasta (1,500–2,000+ m)
slides.1.content: San Juan is led by Syrah, with styles ranging from warm Tulum to high-altitude Pedernal.
slides.2.title: San Rafael
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Location and scale
slides.2.highlights.0.content: About 200–230 km south of Mendoza city, with about 22,000 ha, around 200 wineries and altitudes of about 500–700 m; about 15% of Mendoza's output
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Water and hazards
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Irrigation from Atuel and Diamante river snowmelt; hail risk is real and anti-hail netting is common
slides.2.highlights.2.title: DOC and style
slides.2.highlights.2.content: One of Argentina's two DOCs (the other is Luján de Cuyo); Wine With Seth dates it to 2007 and other sources to the 1990s, so the year is not tested. The style is value-led with soft tannins and ripe fruit
slides.2.content: San Rafael is lower and warmer than the Uco Valley, with value-led wines.
slides.3.title: Patagonia
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Location and scale
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Río Negro, Neuquén and Chubut, from about 39 to 45°S (another section says 38°); about 3,700–4,000 ha, under 2% of the national total; ten IGs and no DOC
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Cool by latitude and wind
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Only 250–700 m; the cool comes from latitude and wind, with westerlies drying the canopy and reducing disease; under 200 mm of rain and an 18–20°C day-night swing
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Pinot Noir and old vines
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Pinot Noir is about 382 ha, 19% of Argentina's Pinot Noir; Bodega Chacra has 2 ha of ungrafted Pinot Noir planted in 1932
slides.3.content: Patagonia gets its coolness from latitude rather than altitude, the reverse of Mendoza's logic.
